# Independent audit: four equal-middle fibers

Audited source: four-fiber-equal-middle-subset-payment-and-plateau-limit.md.



The convex hull of \(A,K,K,C\), with \(A,C\subseteq K\), has exactly those four integer fibers. Every interpolation reaching a middle base stays in \(K\), while endpoint bases are exposed. The selected triple uses the same original ambient cap and opposite endpoint thresholds about its actual middle centroid. It charges the subset theorem once and simply retains nonnegative mass from the unused endpoint.

The numerical comparison
\[
\tfrac12\max(a,c)\ge\tfrac{\Gamma_d}{2}(a+c)
\]
uses only \(\max(a,c)\ge(a+c)/2\) and \(\Gamma_d\le1/2\). Subtracting the target gives the recorded surplus \((1-2\Gamma_d)(a+c)/4\). Vertical and merely containing caps are accounted for. The dimension-one equality possibility is retained.

For equal translated middle bodies, the affine-in-base shear is valid and preserves fiber measure and ambient halfspaces. Each midpoint inclusion then cancels one middle support function and forces the corresponding transformed endpoint inside the common middle body. No endpoint centroid assumption is introduced.

The ten-fiber example has a positive concave radius sequence, exactly the stated mixed hull, and total mass \(23251/2500\). The two prescribed peak centroids fail by the explicitly displayed vertical caps. Base four is a weighted median with the stated strict left and right masses. Since all fiber centroids have continuous coordinate zero, every through-point ambient cap contains a closed half-line of centroids, or all of them when its base coefficient vanishes. Applying ordinary Grünbaum to those actual fibers gives the independent safe-point bound, with vertical caps only stronger.

There is no implied extension from the four-fiber theorem to unrestricted tails or to nonmedian peak selectors. No correction is required.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
